def is_safe_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when name is a plain relative path that stays inside its directory:
    non-empty, not absolute, no NUL, and no `..` component."""
    ex is_safe_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_safe_name("sub/a.txt") == True
    ex is_safe_name("") == False
    ex is_safe_name("../secret.txt") == False
    ex is_safe_name("a/../../b") == False
    ex is_safe_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    if "\0" in name:
        return False
    for part in name.replace("\\", "/").split("/"):
        if part == ".." or part == "":
            return False
    return True

def first_readable(names: list[str]) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the first name in names that can be read as a file inside the
    directory notes (relative to the working directory), or "" when none can.
    Names are untrusted: reads happen under `with fs = fs.sub("notes")`, and
    names failing is_safe_name are skipped. A missing or unreadable file is
    skipped too. Returns "" for an empty list or when nothing is readable."""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        for name in names:
            if not is_safe_name(name):
                continue
            text = fs.read(name) else ""
            if text != "":
                return text
    return ""
